overview: Two-group pragmatic trial in 12 first-opinion practices: dogs are allocated individually 1:1 by a central web system, stratified by practice, to the nurse-led weight clinic or usual vet-led advice, and followed for six months.
population: Dogs aged 2 years or older with osteoarthritis diagnosed by a vet, body condition score 7 or more of 9, whose owners give written consent; excluded are dogs with uncontrolled endocrine disease, dogs expected to need joint surgery within six months, and households unable to attend a six-month review.
exposure: Clinic group: monthly nurse weigh-ins, measured daily food allowance with the discounted therapeutic diet, written exercise plan and a phone check-in between visits. Usual-care group: vet advice and the diet leaflet at the consultation, the same discounted diet available, and one six-month review.
procedures: Vets screen appointment lists weekly; a named nurse champion in each practice approaches owners. After baseline mobility index, weight and a standard lameness video, allocation is obtained from the central web system. At six months every dog, whatever its attendance, has the owner index, weight and a video scored by a vet from another practice who does not know the allocation. Pain relief prescriptions are taken from practice records.

outcomes.name: Owner-reported mobility and comfort
outcomes.measure: Change in the 11-item index (0 to 44, higher worse) from baseline to six months
outcomes.why: The outcome owners value; 4 points is a meaningful change (claim c2).

outcomes.name: Body weight change
outcomes.measure: Percentage change in body weight from baseline
outcomes.why: Objective measure of the clinic's direct effect.

outcomes.name: Blinded lameness score
outcomes.measure: Lameness scored 0 to 4 from standard video by a vet unaware of allocation
outcomes.why: Limits expectation bias in owner reports (claim c3).

outcomes.name: Clinic attendance
outcomes.measure: Proportion of scheduled monthly weigh-ins attended in the clinic group
outcomes.why: Retention is the weak point of weight clinics (claim c4).

outcomes.name: Hunger behaviours
outcomes.measure: Owner report of begging, scavenging or waking for food in the past month

feasibility: About 45 eligible dogs a month are seen; enrolling 45 percent gives about 20 a month, so 120 dogs in six months; two sessions a week per practice are enough for up to 10 clinic dogs per practice.
biasMitigation: Central web allocation stratified by practice
Lameness scored from video by a vet from another practice unaware of allocation
Six-month outcome collected for every dog regardless of attendance
Pain relief changes recorded from practice records, not owner recall

biasFlags.label: Unblinded owners
biasFlags.note: Owner-reported primary outcome is open to expectation; blinded lameness is a check.

biasFlags.label: Attrition
biasFlags.note: Six-month outcome by phone and a single review visit for every dog.

biasFlags.label: Contamination
biasFlags.note: Usual-care owners may hear about the clinic; nurses do not contact them.

flags: Adjustment limited to baseline score, practice and age
parsimony.simplestPath: Two groups, one owner-reported primary outcome, one blinded secondary outcome, six months.

theoreticalFramework: PRECIS-2 to document pragmatism across domains; no behavioural framework beyond the clinic's existing content.
summary: Individually allocated pragmatic trial stratified by practice, with one primary, two secondary, one process and one balancing outcome.
